messages:
sam: Heads-up — noticed our spot-backed inferencer started oscillating after the eu-west-1 batch of evictions this morning. latency p95 spiked and we fired a bunch of on-demand fallback which then scaled back down too fast. anyone else see the pattern?

maria: saw it — logs show 3 eviction waves around 06:12, 06:18, 06:25 UTC. autoscaler reacted to queue length but we got thrash because cold-starts + cooldowns misaligned.

jay: can you paste the autoscaler config used for that pool?

sam: sure — this is the current policy for mixed-capacity pool 

```yaml
policy: mixed_spot_on_demand
scale_out_threshold: 0.65 # queue fill ratio
scale_in_threshold: 0.22
min_replicas: 6
max_replicas: 200
cooldown_seconds: 120
priority_buckets: [spot, ondemand]
```

oliver: cooldown of 120s is too short when cold-start is ~90-120s for some model shards. plus spot eviction causes immediate drop in capacity which looks like a backlog spike and triggers more scale_out. we need a way to distinguish transient backlog from sustained demand.

maria: proposal: introduce an "eviction_buffer" window and a short hold on scale-ins after an eviction event so we don't oscillate between on-demand and spot.

jay: +1. Also consider a small percentage reserve of on-demand (opportunistic-reserve) that only gets used when interruption probability > X or when latency SLO is approaching. cheaper than repeated cold restarts.

sam: sketched a config we could try as a canary for one AZ:

```yaml
policy: mixed_spot_on_demand_opportunistic
scale_out_threshold: 0.7
scale_in_threshold: 0.2
min_replicas: 6
opportunistic_reserve_percent: 8   # keep 8% of desired capacity as ondemand standby
eviction_buffer:
  enabled: true
  hold_for_seconds: 300    # after eviction, delay scale-in for this long
  sliding_window: 60       # aggregate queue signals over this many sec
cooldown_seconds: 240
```

oliver: sounds reasonable. the reserve percent should be adaptive by region — eu-west historically has higher preemption churn vs us-west. maybe tie reserve to measured interruption_rate metric.

maria: agree. we can compute reserve_pct = clamp( floor(interruption_rate * 1.5), 2, 15 ) — keeps it small in calm regions and larger in high-churn zones.

sam: operational checklist for canary rollout:
- pick eu-west-1a (low traffic canary)
- enable policy on one pool (tag: canary-evict-buffer)
- run for 48h, track p95 latency, tokens/sec, on-demand usage, cold-starts - alert if on-demand cost > 20% above baseline or p95 > SLO

jay: add a dashboard panel for "eviction_event_count" and "reserve_usage_pct". infra-bot can post daily summary to #eng-infra.

infra-bot: deployed metric collectors: eviction_event_count, interruption_rate, reserve_usage_pct to prometheus.canary namespace. will post daily at 08:00 UTC.

eng-oncall: just flagging net constraints too — eu-west had a transient routing flap earlier which made some kube nodes appear NotReady for ~40s. combined with evictions, that's part of the story. worth excluding network-induced NRs from eviction metric via node annotations.

maria: good catch. we'll filter node_status.reason != "NetworkUnreachable" when calculating interruption_rate for reserve sizing.

sam: one more thought — introduce "compaction windows" on scale-in where we prefer to reduce spot replicas first and only act on ondemand if spot count is healthy. reduces churn on ondemand. pseudocode: 

```text
if desired_replicas < current_replicas:
  drop_spot_first = true
  if (time_since_last_eviction < eviction_buffer.hold_for_seconds) then skip_ondemand_scale_in
```

oliver: that matches my expectation. also add a jittered scale-in delay per-pod to avoid synchronized drains.

jay: how about costs? keeping a reserve increases spend but reduces repeated cold-start CPU/GPU overhead. we should run a 7d cost model sim comparing: baseline (no reserve), fixed reserve 8%, adaptive reserve.

maria: I'll run the sim. quick back-of-envelope: one extra on-demand G4 in eu-west is ~X/day; but each cold-start surge we've been seeing triggers ~3 on-demand nodes for ~10min each — could be cost neutral or saving depending on frequency.

sam: ok let's spin canary tomorrow 06:00 UTC, maria will run cost sim, oliver will add jittered drain, jay will add dashboard panels. if sms/alert thresholds hit, infra-bot to auto-revert.

infra-bot: scheduled rollout: canary-evict-buffer -> 2026-03-19 06:00:00 UTC. auto-revert on cost_delta > 0.20 within 12h or p95 breach > SLO.

eng-oncall: will standby during initial 6h window. ping me on pager if anything spikes.

sam: thanks — let's keep the thread for post-canary notes. short-term win if we can stop the thrash and keep cost steady. :crossed_fingers:
